Yoga is like a fun exercise game for your body and your mind at the same time.

You make slow, stretchy shapes with your body called poses. You might stand tall and still like a tree, stretch up big like a mountain, or curl up small like a cat. While you hold each shape, you take slow, deep breaths in and out through your nose. This helps your brain feel calm and focused.

You don't have to be super bendy to do yoga. You just listen to your body, try your best, and pay attention to how you feel. It can help you feel strong, peaceful, and happy!

Learning a new language is like getting a secret superpower!

At first, you already have one language that lets you talk to your family and friends. Learning a new one is like getting a second key that can unlock new doors.

Here's how it works:

1.  **You start with building blocks.** Just like in a video game, you learn the small pieces first - how to say "hello," "thank you," "my name is..." and words for things you love, like pizza or dinosaurs.

2.  **It's okay to sound silly.** You will say words funny at first and you might mix them up. That's totally normal! Every kid who learns a new language does that. It's like learning to ride a bike - you wobble a lot before you can ride fast.

3.  **Your brain gets stronger.** When you practice, your brain makes new roads called connections. The more you listen, speak, and play in the new language - like watching cartoons, singing songs, or playing games - the stronger those roads get.

4.  **And then magic happens.** One day, you'll understand a joke, or make a new friend, or watch a movie without needing anyone to translate. You can talk to way more people in the world!

It doesn't happen in one day. It takes little bits of practice every day, just like practicing soccer or piano. But it's a fun adventure.

Stay curious

A smartphone is like a superpower — it's super fun, but you have to use it wisely!

Here are 4 smart rules for a 10-year-old superhero like you:

**1. Time Boss:** Don't let the phone boss you around. It's good to play games and watch videos, but also make time to play outside, read, hang out with family and friends, and sleep. A good trick is: no phone at dinner and no phone 1 hour before bed.

**2. Safety First:** Never share your full name, school name, address, or photos with people you don't know in real life. If a stranger messages you or something makes you feel weird or scared, tell a trusted grown-up right away. That's always the right thing to do.

**3. Be Kind:** Only type things you would say to someone's face. No mean comments, no forwarding embarrassing pictures. Remember there's a real person with feelings on the other side of the screen.

**4. Think Before You Click:** Not everything online is true, and some apps want to trick you into spending money or watching too much. Always ask a parent before downloading a new app or clicking on a pop-up ad.

Use it to learn, create, laugh, and connect — and then put it down and enjoy the real world too!

Saving money is choosing to not spend everything you earn today so you have more security tomorrow. It means setting aside a portion of your income, even a small amount, instead of using it for immediate wants. Interestingly, you can grow your own yummy vegetables right at home, even if you don't have a big farm!

Think of a plant like a tiny green factory. It needs four things to work: sunlight, water, soil, and air.

Here is how you can start your own little garden:

1.  **Pick an easy vegetable:** For beginners, great choices are cherry tomatoes, lettuce, carrots, or radishes. They grow pretty fast!
2.  **Find a sunny spot:** Most vegetables love sunshine. Find a place near a window, on a balcony, or in your yard that gets at least 6 hours of sun a day.
3.  **Get a container and soil:** You can use a pot, an old bucket with holes in the bottom, or a small patch of ground in your yard. Fill it with potting soil from a garden store — it's like super-food for plants.
4.  **Plant the seeds:** Make a little hole with your finger, drop the seed in, and lightly cover it with soil. Check the seed packet to see how deep it should be.
5.  **Water and wait:** Gently water your soil so it stays damp like a wrung-out sponge, not too soggy. Now the magic happens! The seed will sprout into a tiny seedling.
6.  **Be patient and care for it:** Keep watering it a little every day and make sure it gets lots of sun. Pull out any weeds (plants you didn't plant) so your vegetable doesn't have to share its food and water.

After a few weeks or months, your plant will be big enough to give you real vegetables you can pick and eat. Isn't it cool to eat something you grew yourself?

Think of your body like a super cool water balloon that's always moving!

About half of your body is actually made of water, and you need to keep topping it up to feel your best.

Here's what water does for you:

**1. It gives you energy to play:** When you run, jump, and play, your muscles need water to work. If you don't drink enough, you might feel tired and grumpy.

**2. It helps your brain think:** Your brain loves water. Drinking enough helps you focus in school, remember things, and solve problems.

**3. It keeps you cool:** When you get hot and sweaty, water helps cool your whole body down, like an inside air-conditioner.

**4. It's great for your health:** Water helps your tummy digest food, keeps your skin soft, and helps carry good things from food all around your body.

How do you know if you're drinking enough?
*   Feel thirsty? That's your body's way of saying "time for a drink!"
*   Check your pee. If it's light yellow, like lemonade, you're doing great. If it's dark yellow, like apple juice, drink some more water.
*   Try to drink water with every meal and whenever you are playing hard or it's hot outside. A good goal is about 4 to 6 glasses a day, but your body will tell you what it needs.

Water is way more fun than soda because it has no sugar and still does all the awesome jobs above!

Hi there! I'm happy to explain how to take great care of a pet.

Having a pet is like having a new best friend who lives with you. They depend on you for almost everything, just like a little brother or sister would.

Here are the big jobs of a pet owner:

**1. Yummy Food and Fresh Water**
Pets need the right food every day, and clean water all the time. Dogs can't eat chocolate, and cats can't drink lots of milk — so always ask a grown-up what is safe for your pet.

**2. A Cozy, Clean Home**
Your pet needs a safe place to sleep and go to the bathroom. That means cleaning a litter box for a cat, cleaning a cage for a hamster or bunny, taking a dog out for potty walks, or cleaning a fish tank.

**3. Exercise and Playtime**
Pets get bored just like you do! Dogs love walks and fetch, cats love chasing toys, and even bunnies and hamsters need time to hop and explore. Playing with them keeps them healthy and happy.

**4. Doctor Check-ups**
Pets need to visit the vet, which is an animal doctor. The vet gives them shots to keep them from getting sick and checks their teeth, ears, and weight.

**5. Love and Kindness**
This is the most important job! Be gentle, use a calm voice, and learn what your pet likes. Never tease, hit, or chase them when they are scared. If you are kind, they will love and trust you.

If you feed them, keep them clean, play with them, and give them lots of love, you will be an awesome pet owner!

Hey! Let's talk about why sleep is like a superpower for you.

Think of your brain like a phone that you use all day for learning, playing, and talking to friends. By nighttime, its battery is low. Sleep is what plugs you in to recharge to 100% so you're ready to go again tomorrow.

While you're sleeping, amazing things are happening inside you:

1. **Your brain gets smarter.** It takes everything you learned at school, like math and spelling, and saves it so you remember it.
2. **Your body grows stronger.** Sleep releases special growth juice that helps your muscles, bones, and immune system. That's what helps you not get sick and grow tall.
3. **Your mood gets happier.** Have you ever felt grumpy after staying up late? Good sleep helps you feel happy, calm, and ready to have fun and be kind to others.

Most 10-year-olds need about 9 to 11 hours of sleep every night. That means if you have to wake up at 7 in the morning, you should be asleep around 8 or 9 at night.

So getting enough sleep helps you run faster, think clearer, learn better, and feel great!

Hey there! Have you ever wondered why you have to go to sleep every night, even when you want to stay up and play? Sleep might seem boring, but it's actually like a superpower for your body and brain!

Here’s what sleep does for you:

**1. It helps your brain learn and remember**
During the day you learn so much at school, from playing, and from talking with friends. When you sleep, your brain sorts through everything you learned and saves it, like saving a video game. That’s why you can remember things better after a good night’s sleep!

**2. It helps your body grow strong**
When you are sleeping deeply, your body makes a special growth juice that helps you get taller and stronger, and fixes any boo-boos like scraped knees. It's like having a tiny repair crew working while you snooze.

**3. It gives you energy and a good mood**
Have you noticed how cranky and tired you feel when you don't sleep enough? A full night of sleep (about 9 to 11 hours for a kid your age) charges you up like a battery. You can run faster, play longer, think more clearly, and feel happier.

**4. It keeps you healthy and safe**
Sleep helps your body fight off germs so you don’t get sick as often. And when you are well-rested, you can pay better attention so you don’t get hurt while playing or riding your bike.

So getting to bed on time, sleeping in a dark, cool room, and not looking at tablets right before bed are all great ways to get awesome super-sleep!

A smartphone is like a super-powered tool that fits in your pocket. It can be really helpful and fun, but it's important to use it wisely, like you would with a bike or a pet!

Here are some wise ways to use a smartphone:

**1. Use it as a Tool, Not Just a Toy**
A phone is great for learning, talking to family, looking things up for school, and finding directions. Games and funny videos are fun, but they shouldn't be the only thing you do on it.

**2. Take Breaks**
Staring at a screen for too long can hurt your eyes, make it hard to sleep, and give you a headache. Remember the 20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something far away for 20 seconds. And never take your phone to bed with you — your brain needs rest without a screen!

**3. Balance Your Time**
Life is more fun when you have a mix of things. Make sure you still have time to play outside, read books, do homework, help at home, and hang out with friends face-to-face. Try not to use your phone when you're eating with family or talking to someone.

**4. Be Safe and Private**
Never share private information like your full name, address, school name, passwords, or photos with people online, especially people you don't know in real life. If a stranger messages you or something feels weird or scary, tell a trusted adult right away.

**5. Be Kind and Think Before You Post**
Don't say anything online that you wouldn't say to someone's face. Once you send a message or photo, it's hard to take it back. Always be kind, and if you see someone being mean online, don't join in — tell an adult.

**6. Ask for Help**
If you're not sure if an app is safe, if you want to download something new, or if you see something that upsets you, always ask a parent, teacher, or another trusted adult. They are there to help you!

When you use your smartphone in these wise ways, it can be an amazing helper for you!

Sleep is like a superpower for your body and brain!

Think of your body like a phone that you use all day for playing, learning, and running around. By the end of the day, its battery is low. Sleep is how you plug yourself in to recharge.

Here's what sleep does for you:

**1. It helps your brain learn and remember.** While you sleep, your brain sorts everything you learned at school that day, like filing papers into folders, so you can remember it better tomorrow.

**2. It helps your body grow strong.** When you sleep, your body makes a special growth helper that makes your muscles and bones stronger and taller. That's why kids need more sleep than grown-ups!

**3. It fixes your body.** If you got a scrape or were tired from playing soccer, sleep gives your body time to repair itself.

**4. It makes your mood better.** Have you ever felt grumpy when you didn't sleep enough? A good night's sleep helps you feel happy, patient, and ready to have fun and be kind to friends and family. It also helps you pay attention so you don't feel sleepy in class.

Most 10-year-olds need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep each night to feel their best. So going to bed at a regular time, even when you don't feel super tired, is one of the best things you can do for yourself!

A smartphone is like a super-powered mini computer that fits in your pocket. It can be really helpful and fun, but it's important to use it wisely, like you would with any powerful tool!

Here are some wise ways to use it:

**1. Use it as a tool, not just a toy**
A smartphone is great for learning new things, like watching science videos, reading about animals, or learning how to draw. Try to use it to create and learn, not just to scroll and watch for hours.

**2. Take lots of breaks**
Staring at a screen for too long can make your eyes tired and your body stiff. Remember the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds. And don't forget to go outside, play, and move your body!

**3. Protect your sleep and your brain**
Your brain needs rest to grow. Don't use your phone right before bedtime — the bright light can make it hard to fall asleep. Keep it charging outside your bedroom at night.

**4. Keep private things private**
Never share your full name, address, school name, passwords, or photos of yourself with people you don't know online. If a game or app asks for this, always ask a grown-up first. People online are not always who they say they are.

**5. Be kind and be careful**
Only say things online that you would say kindly to someone's face. If you see something scary, mean, or confusing, close it and tell a trusted adult right away — you will not get in trouble.

**6. Ask a grown-up to be your teammate**
Your parents or guardians are there to help. Let them know what apps you use, set screen time rules together, and ask them before downloading anything new.

Think of your smartphone like a bicycle — it's amazing when you learn to ride it safely, wear a helmet, and follow the rules!

Thank you for reading

Don't be afraid of mistakes: even native speakers mess up! Mistakes help you learn.
Use it a little every day: ten minutes is better than one big hour once a week.
Find a buddy: practice with a friend, family member, or teacher.

Keep practicing, have fun, and Stay curious

Remember saving money is like putting your extra game tokens aside for later instead of using them all right now.

Imagine you get $10 for allowance or a birthday gift. You could spend it all today on candy and small toys, and then it would be gone. But if you save it, you put some of that money in a safe place like a piggy bank or a savings account at a bank. Saving means you are keeping money to use in the future.

People save for three big reasons:

1.  **To buy something bigger later:** If you want a $50 video game or a new bike, you can save $10 each week until you have enough.
2.  **For emergencies:** If your favorite toy breaks and you need to replace it, you'll be happy you have money saved.
3.  **To watch it grow:** If you keep money in a bank, the bank will actually pay you a little extra money called interest just for keeping it there. So your money grows by itself!

A fun trick is to split your money into three jars: one for Spending Now, one for Saving for Later, and one for Sharing or Giving. That way you can still enjoy some money today while you build up money for tomorrow.

Saving teaches you patience and helps you get the things you really, really want the most.

Think of your body like a plant or like a superhero suit that you wear every day.

Your body is made of more than half water! You lose water all day when you sweat, go to the bathroom, and even when you breathe.

When you drink enough water, you help your body do its jobs:

*   **You get more energy** to run, play, and focus at school. When you don't drink enough, you might feel tired or get a headache.
*   **Your brain works better.** Water helps you think clearly and remember things.
*   **It keeps you cool.** When you run around and get hot, water helps cool you down.
*   **It keeps your tummy happy** and helps your body use food to stay strong and keep your **health** in great shape.

How do you know if you're drinking enough?

1.  Drink when you feel thirsty - that's your body's way of saying "I need water!"
2.  Try to sip water throughout the day, especially when it's hot or after playing sports.
3.  Check the color of your pee. If it's light yellow like lemonade, you're doing great. If it's dark yellow like apple juice, you need to drink more water.

Water is the best choice. Sodas and juice have lots of sugar, but plain water gives you everything you need with no extra sugar.

Try keeping a reusable water bottle with you so you can take sips whenever you need to!

A smartphone is a powerful little computer that can fit in your pocket. It can be super helpful and fun, but it's important to use it wisely, like you would with any powerful tool!

Here are some smart rules for using a smartphone:

**1. It's a Tool, Not a Toy All Day**
Use it to learn new things, talk to family, and create cool stuff. But also make sure you spend lots of time playing outside, reading books, drawing, and hanging out with friends in person. Your eyes and brain need breaks from the screen!

**2. Time Limits Are Your Friend**
It's easy to watch videos or play games and lose track of time. Set a timer, like 30 minutes or an hour a day, and stick to it. When the timer rings, put the phone down and do something else.

**3. Be Safe and Kind**
*   Never share private information like your address, school name, or passwords with anyone online.
*   Only talk to people you know in real life. If a stranger messages you, tell a grown-up you trust right away.
*   Be kind online, just like you are in person. Don't say anything online you wouldn't say face-to-face.
*   If you see something that makes you feel weird, scared, or uncomfortable, close it and tell a parent or teacher immediately.

**4. Ask First**
Always ask a parent or guardian before you download a new app or game, buy something, or click on a new website.

Using your phone wisely means you stay in control of it, instead of letting it control you!

Remember saving money is like keeping some of your candy for later instead of eating it all right now.

Imagine you get $10 for your birthday. You could spend it all on toys today, and then it's gone. Or you could split it up like pizza slices:

1. Spend a little now for something fun
2. Save a little for something BIG later, like a bike or a video game
3. Share a little to help someone else

When you save, you put your money somewhere safe, like a piggy bank or a bank account. Every time you add a dollar, your savings grow bigger and bigger, like building with LEGO blocks.

The cool trick is: the longer you wait and keep saving, the more amazing thing you can get later. It's being kind to Future You!

So start small, be patient, and watch your money grow. Thank you for reading

Interestingly, growing vegetables at home is like having tiny green pets that you take care of, except you get to eat them later!

First you pick something easy and fast to grow, like cherry tomatoes, carrots, lettuce, or beans. You put some soft soil in a pot or a little garden box, poke a tiny hole with your finger, drop in a seed, and gently cover it up.

Then your plants need three big things: sunshine, water, and patience. Put them where they get lots of sun, like a windowsill or balcony. Give them a little drink of water every day so the soil feels damp like a wrung-out sponge, but not swampy. In a few days or weeks, you will see a tiny sprout pop up, and then leaves, and then your veggie!

Just remember to pull out weeds, watch for hungry bugs, and wait until your vegetables look big and colorful before you pick them. It is so cool to eat something you grew yourself. That is all for today

Honestly, preparing for exams is a lot like training for a big game or practicing for a talent show.

You wouldn't just show up without practice, right? You'd practice a little bit every day so your brain and body remember what to do.

Here are three simple tricks to get ready:

1.  **Don't cram, make a plan.** Instead of trying to learn everything in one night, study a little bit each day. Like 20 minutes of math on Monday, 20 minutes of science on Tuesday. It's much easier for your brain!

2.  **Make it active and fun.** Don't just stare at your notes. Turn them into quiz cards, draw silly pictures to remember facts, or pretend you're the teacher and explain the lesson to a stuffed animal. If you can teach it, you really know it!

3.  **Take care of your brain's battery.** Your brain needs sleep to save what you learned, healthy snacks and water for energy, and short breaks to play and move around. Studying for 25 minutes then taking a 5-minute break works super well.

You got this! Exams just show what you've learned, they don't show how awesome and creative you are.

A smartphone is like a superpower tool — it can help you learn, play, talk to family, and be creative. But just like a bike or a skateboard, you have to use it safely and wisely!

Here are 5 smart rules:

**1. Use it with a purpose**
Ask yourself: *What am I using it for?* Learning something new, calling grandma, taking photos, or playing for a little bit are all great reasons. Try not to just scroll and scroll without thinking.

**2. Take breaks**
Your eyes, body, and brain need rest. Follow the 30-30 rule: after 30 minutes, put the phone down, stretch, drink water, go outside, or play with something else.

**3. Keep private things private**
Never share your full name, school, address, passwords, or photos of yourself without asking a trusted grown-up first. Once something is on the internet, it's very hard to take back.

**4. Be kind and be careful**
Only say nice things you would say face-to-face. If a message, video, or game makes you feel scared, sad, or weird, close it and tell a parent or teacher right away. That's always the right thing to do.

**5. Phone-free times**
Phones need to sleep too! Keep it away during meals, homework, playing with friends, and at bedtime. You’ll sleep better and have more fun.

When you use your phone this way, you’re the boss of it — it’s not the boss of you!

Think of your body like a plant!

A plant needs water to stand up tall, grow, and stay green. Your body needs water for the same kind of reasons.

Here is what water does for you:

**1. It gives you energy to play**
About half of your body is made of water! When you drink enough, you can run, jump, and think more clearly. When you don't drink enough, you might feel tired, get a headache, or feel grumpy.

**2. It keeps everything running smoothly**
Water helps your body digest food, keeps your skin healthy, and helps you cool down when you sweat on a hot day or during sports. It's also really good for your health!

**3. It helps clean you out**
When you drink water, it helps your body flush out the stuff it doesn't need when you go to the bathroom.

### How do you know if you're drinking enough?

* **Listen to your thirst.** If your mouth feels dry or sticky, it's time for a drink.
* **Check the color of your pee.** If it's pale yellow, like lemonade, you're doing great. If it's dark yellow, like apple juice, drink more water.
* **Make it a habit.** Drink a glass with every meal, and bring a water bottle to school and to practice.

You don't have to only drink plain water - fruits like watermelon and oranges have lots of water in them too! But water is the best choice, much better than soda or juice with lots of sugar.

Try to sip water little by little all day long, instead of drinking a huge amount all at once.

Interestingly, you can grow your own yummy vegetables right at home, even if you don't have a big garden!

Think of a plant like a tiny factory. It needs four important things to make vegetables: sunlight, water, soil, and air.

1. **Sunlight:** Plants are like tiny superheroes that get their power from the sun. Find a sunny spot near a window, on a balcony, or in your backyard where the sun shines for at least 6 hours a day.

2. **Soil:** Plants need cozy, fluffy soil to stretch their roots. You can use pots, old buckets, or a small patch of ground. Make sure the soil is soft and has good food for plants, called compost.

3. **Seeds or Seedlings:** You can start with tiny seeds or a little baby plant from a garden store. Easy vegetables for beginners are tomatoes, lettuce, radishes, and carrots. Just make a little hole in the soil, put the seed in, and cover it lightly.

4. **Water and Love:** Give your plants a drink of water every day or two, but don't drown them! The soil should feel damp like a wrung-out sponge. And be patient. You also need to pull out any weeds, which are unwanted plants that try to steal food and water.

After a few weeks, you will see a little green sprout pop up! Keep taking care of it, and that sprout will grow bigger and finally give you fresh vegetables you can pick and eat. There's nothing better than eating something you grew yourself!

Honestly, preparing for exams is a lot like training for a big game or getting ready for a big performance.

You wouldn't just show up on game day without practicing, right? Your brain needs practice too!

Here are a few simple tricks to get ready:

1.  **Don't cram, make a plan.** Instead of trying to learn everything the night before, study a little bit each day. It's like eating your dinner in small bites instead of trying to swallow it all at once. 20 or 30 minutes a day is much better than 3 hours the night before.

2.  **Make it fun and active.** Don't just stare at your notes. Quiz yourself with flashcards, explain the topic out loud to a teddy bear or a family member, or draw colorful pictures and maps about what you're learning. When you teach it to someone else, you really know it!

3.  **Take brain breaks.** Your brain gets tired! Study for a little while, then take a 5-minute break to stretch, drink water, or get some fresh air. Then come back and your brain will be ready again.

4.  **Sleep and snack smart.** On the night before the exam, get a good night's sleep. Your brain saves everything you learned while you sleep! And eat a good breakfast so your brain has energy for the test.

Remember, an exam just shows what you've learned so far. If you prepare a little every day, you'll feel calm and confident when the test comes.

Taking care of a pet is like being a good best friend to them!

Pets need you to help them stay happy and healthy every day. Here is what that means:

**1. Good Food and Fresh Water**
Give your pet the right food every day, and make sure they always have clean water to drink. Don't give them human snacks like chocolate or chips, because those can make them sick.

**2. A Clean, Cozy Home**
Whether it's a fish tank, a dog crate, a bird cage, or a litter box for a cat, keep their home clean. Give them a soft, warm place to sleep.

**3. Play and Exercise**
Pets need to move and play, just like you do! Play fetch with a dog, dangle a toy for a cat, or let a hamster run on its wheel. This keeps them strong and happy.

**4. Doctor Check-ups**
Pets need to visit the animal doctor, called a vet. The vet gives them shots to keep them from getting sick and makes sure they are growing well.

**5. Lots of Love and Kindness**
Be gentle, pet them nicely, and never yell at or scare them. Learn what they like. A happy pet will wag its tail, purr, or chirp to show they love you back!

If you feed them, keep them clean, play with them, and love them, you will be an awesome pet owner. That is all for today

Interestingly, growing vegetables at home is like having a tiny magic garden where you turn little seeds into yummy food!

First, you pick what you want to grow. Easy ones for beginners are tomatoes, carrots, lettuce, and beans. They grow fast and are fun to watch.

Next, you need a sunny spot, because plants love sunshine like we love pizza. It gives them energy to grow big and strong. A windowsill, balcony, or backyard all work great.

Then you get some soil and a pot or a garden box with little holes at the bottom so extra water can drain out. You poke a small hole in the soil with your finger, drop in a seed, and gently cover it up like tucking it into bed.

Now comes the important part: water and patience. You water them a little bit every day, just enough to keep the soil damp like a wrung-out sponge, not swimming like a pool. Then you wait and watch. In a few days, a tiny green sprout will pop up. How cool is that?

You keep watering and make sure they get lots of sun. You can also pull out any weeds, which are sneaky plants you did not plant. After a few weeks or months, your vegetables will be big enough to pick and eat!

You grew that yourself, which makes it taste even better. That is all for today

Having a pet is like having a best friend who lives with you! But pets can't take care of themselves, so it's your job to help them stay happy and healthy.

Here is what pets need every day:

**1. Yummy Food and Fresh Water**
Just like you need breakfast, lunch, and dinner, your pet does too. Make sure they get the right food for their kind of animal — dog food for dogs, cat food for cats, hay and veggies for bunnies — and clean water every day.

**2. A Clean, Cozy Home**
Pets need a safe place to sleep and play. That means cleaning out a fish tank, washing a dog bed, changing litter for a cat, or cleaning shavings for a hamster.

**3. Playtime and Exercise**
Pets get bored just like kids do! Play fetch with your dog, dangle a toy for your cat, or let your lizard explore safely. It keeps them strong and happy.

**4. Love and Kindness**
Be gentle, use a calm voice, and never tease or hurt them. Learn what they like — belly rubs, chin scratches, or just sitting near you.

**5. Doctor Visits**
Just like you go to the doctor, pets go to the vet. They need check-ups and shots to stay healthy.

When you take good care of a pet, they will trust you and love you a whole lot back. That is all for today

Interestingly, growing vegetables at home is super fun and easy, kind of like a science experiment you can eat!

First pick something simple, like cherry tomatoes, lettuce, carrots, or green beans. They grow fast and don't need a big yard — a sunny windowsill, balcony, or small garden patch works great.

You need four main things:
1. Sunshine: Most veggies love 6 hours of sun a day.
2. Soil: Soft, dark soil with compost helps roots stretch out.
3. Water: Keep soil damp like a wrung-out sponge, not soggy like a puddle.
4. Patience: Seeds sprout in a week or two, then you watch leaves get bigger every day.

Plant the seed about as deep as your fingertip, give it water, and check on it daily. Pull out weeds that steal food and water, and say hello to helpful bugs like ladybugs.

In a few weeks or months you can pick your own fresh snack right off the plant. It tastes extra yummy because you grew it yourself. That is all for today

Interestingly you can grow your own yummy vegetables right at home, even if you don't have a big farm!

Think of a plant like a little factory that needs four things to make food: sunshine, water, air, and soil.

1. **Pick a vegetable:** Start with easy ones that grow fast, like lettuce, radishes, cherry tomatoes, or carrots. You can even grow green beans in a small cup!

2. **Find a sunny spot:** Most vegetables love sunshine. Find a place near a window, on a balcony, or in your yard that gets at least 6 hours of sun a day.

3. **Get some soil and a pot:** You can use a real garden bed, or just a pot with holes in the bottom so extra water can drain out. Fill it with potting soil from a store — it's super fluffy and healthy for plants.

4. **Plant the seeds:** Read the packet to see how deep to plant them. Usually you poke a little hole with your finger, drop the seed in, and cover it lightly with soil. Then give it a gentle drink of water.

5. **Water and wait:** Keep the soil damp like a wrung-out sponge, not swimming like a pool. Every day check your plant. In a week or two, you will see a tiny green sprout pop up — that's your plant being born!

6. **Be patient and helpful:** Pull out any weeds (plants you didn't plant), and watch for hungry bugs. Soon your sprout will grow bigger, make flowers, and then grow the vegetable you can eat.

The best part is harvesting and eating what YOU grew — it tastes extra delicious!

That is all for today

Taking care of a pet is a big and important job, because a pet depends on you for everything!

Here is what it means to be a great pet owner:

**1. Food and Water:** Just like you need breakfast, lunch, and dinner, your pet needs fresh food and clean water every single day. Make sure you give them the right kind of food for their animal — dogs, cats, fish, and hamsters all eat different things!

**2. A Clean and Safe Home:** Your pet needs a cozy, safe place to sleep and live. For a dog or cat that might be a soft bed, for a hamster a clean cage, and for a fish a clean tank. You have to help clean up after them, too.

**3. Exercise and Playtime:** Pets need to move and have fun! Dogs need walks and games of fetch, cats love to chase toys, and even small pets like bunnies need time to hop around. Playing with them keeps them happy and healthy.

**4. Health and Doctor Visits:** Pets can't tell us when they feel sick, so you have to watch them closely. They need to visit the animal doctor, called a vet, for check-ups and shots to keep them from getting sick. You also need to keep them clean by brushing them.

**5. Love and Attention:** The most important thing is to give your pet lots of love, kindness, and patience. Pet them, talk to them nicely, and never be mean to them. When you love your pet, they will love you back a whole lot!

Having a pet is like having a best friend who will always be there for you if you take good care of them.

That is all for today

Hey there! Let's talk about sleep — it's like a superpower for your body and brain!

Think of your brain like a phone that you use all day for school, playing, and learning new things. By bedtime, your battery is super low. Sleep is plugging yourself in to charge back up to 100%!

Here’s what happens while you’re snoozing:

**1. Your Brain Saves What You Learned**
During the day you learn math, reading, and cool facts. At night, while you sleep, your brain files all of that away so you can remember it. Sleeping helps you get better grades and learn faster!

**2. Your Body Grows Strong**
When you are in deep sleep, your body releases a special grow-juice that helps your muscles, bones, and even cuts or bruises get stronger and heal. That’s why kids need more sleep than grown-ups — you’re still growing!

**3. You Get Better Feelings and Energy**
Have you ever felt super grumpy or cranky when you stayed up too late? That’s because your brain didn’t get to rest. A good night’s sleep helps you feel happy, be kind to friends, and have tons of energy to run and play the next day. It even helps you not get sick!

So try to get 9 to 11 hours of sleep every night. That means no bright screens right before bed, a cool dark room, and going to bed around the same time.

Sleep isn’t boring time when nothing happens — it’s when your body does its most awesome secret work!

That is all for today

Honestly preparing for exams is a lot like getting ready for a big soccer game or a fun performance.

You wouldn't just show up and hope for the best, right? You would practice a little bit every day.

Here is how you can do it:

1. Start early and do little bits. Reading for 20 minutes each day is way better than trying to learn everything in one long, tired night.

2. Make it fun and active. Don't just stare at the page. Draw pictures, make flashcards, sing a song about it, or pretend you are the teacher explaining it to a teddy bear.

3. Sleep and snack smart. Your brain is like a superhero battery. It needs good sleep, water, and yummy healthy food to work its best.

4. It's okay to feel nervous. Even grown-ups do. Just take three slow deep breaths, and remember that a test just shows what you know right now, it doesn't show how awesome and smart you are.

Yoga is like a fun game for your body and your mind at the same time!

Imagine you get to pretend to be different things - a tall tree with your arms stretched up high, a sleepy cat stretching its back, or a strong warrior. You make these shapes with your **body** by stretching and balancing.

While you hold the shapes, you also practice breathing slowly and deeply, in and out through your nose. This helps you feel calm and focused, like when you take a deep breath before a big test.

You don't need to be bendy or perfect to do yoga. You just move gently, listen to how your body feels, and try your best. It can help you feel strong, flexible, calm, and happy, and it's a great way to relax if you feel wiggly or worried.

It's usually done on a soft mat, with no shoes, and you can do it at home, in a park, or in a class with a teacher.

Think of your body like a super cool water slide park!

About half of your body is made of water. That water is busy all day helping you run, think, and play.

When you drink enough water, good things happen:

**You get more energy for play.** Water helps carry fuel to your muscles and brain, so you don't feel tired and grumpy in the middle of a game.

**Your brain thinks clearer.** Ever feel fuzzy or get a headache on a hot day? Sometimes that means your brain is thirsty! A glass of water can help you focus better on schoolwork or video games.

**It keeps your whole body working.** Water helps your tummy digest pizza, helps keep you cool when you sweat, and is great for your health, skin, and teeth.

How do you know if you drank enough? Check your pee! If it's light yellow like lemonade, you're doing great. If it's dark yellow like apple juice, go grab some water.

Try to sip water through the day, not just when you're really thirsty. Keep a fun water bottle with you at school, take a few sips after recess, and drink extra when it's hot or you're playing sports.

Your body will thank you with more zoom-zoom power!

Taking care of a pet is a big responsibility, because a pet depends on you for everything, just like a younger brother or sister would!

Here are the most important jobs of a pet owner:

**1. Food and Water**
Pets need fresh, clean water every day and the right kind of food for their body. You can't give a dog chocolate or give a cat dog food - each pet needs its own special healthy food, and not too much or too little.

**2. A Safe and Clean Home**
Your pet needs a cozy, safe place to sleep and relax. For a dog or cat that might be a warm bed, for a fish it's a clean tank, and for a hamster it's a cage with soft bedding. You have to help keep their space clean by washing bowls, changing litter boxes, or cleaning cages.

**3. Love and Attention**
Pets need love, kindness, and playtime every day! Playing with them, petting them gently, and talking to them helps them feel happy and safe. They should never be hit or yelled at.

**4. Exercise and Fun**
Dogs need walks and games like fetch, cats love to chase toys, and even birds and hamsters need time outside their cage to explore and play. Exercise keeps them healthy and not bored.

**5. Health and Safety**
Pets need to visit the animal doctor, called a veterinarian or vet, for check-ups and shots to keep them from getting sick. You also need to keep them safe by keeping doors and gates closed so they don't run away, and keeping dangerous things like cleaning supplies away from them.

If you do all these things, your pet will be happy, healthy, and will love you a lot in return!

A smartphone is like a superpower tool - it can help you learn, play, talk to family, and be creative. But just like a bike or a skateboard, you have to use it safely and wisely!

Here are 5 smart rules for a 10-year-old:

1. **Time is precious.** Don't stare at your phone all day. It's more fun to play outside, read, draw, or hang out with friends and family. Try setting a timer so your phone doesn't steal your playtime.

2. **Ask before you tap.** Always ask a parent or trusted grown-up before you download a new app, buy something, or click on a weird pop-up. Some things cost money or can be unsafe.

3. **Be kind online.** Only send messages or photos you would be happy to show your grandma. Never be mean, and if someone is mean to you, tell a trusted adult right away. Don't delete the message so they can help.

4. **Stranger danger is real on phones too.** Never share your full name, address, school name, passwords, or photos with someone you met in a game or online. Real friends don't ask for private information.

5. **Put it to sleep.** Phones need rest and so do you! Don't use your phone during meals, homework, or family time, and charge it outside your bedroom at night so you sleep well.

When you use your phone to learn new things, help others, and have fun in balance, you're being a wise smartphone superstar!

Learning a new language is like getting a superpower!

At first, you only know one way to say things, like "Hello" or "I love pizza." But when you learn a new language, you learn a whole new code to say the same things. "Hello" might become "Hola" in Spanish or "Bonjour" in French.

It's a lot like learning the rules to a new game:

1.  **You learn new sounds:** Your mouth has to make shapes it has never made before. It can feel silly at first, like doing a tongue workout!
2.  **You learn new words:** It's like collecting stickers. Each new word is a sticker you can use to build bigger and bigger sentences.
3.  **You get to connect with more people:** It's like unlocking a new level where you can make new friends, understand movies or songs, and feel at home in a different country.

You won't be perfect at first, and that's okay! You will mix up words and make funny mistakes. That's just part of the adventure. The more you practice by listening, speaking, and playing with the language, the easier it gets.

Honestly, preparing for an exam is a lot like training for a big game or practicing for a talent show.

You wouldn't just show up on the day without practicing, right? Your brain needs practice too!

Here’s how you can do it in a simple, stress-free way:

1.  **Start early and do a little at a time.** It's much better to study for 20 minutes every day than to try to learn everything the night before. Your brain remembers better when it sleeps in between practice times.

2.  **Make it active and fun.** Don't just stare at your notes. Try things like making colorful flashcards, drawing pictures of what you learned, answering practice questions, or pretending you are the teacher and explaining it to a stuffed animal or a family member.

3.  **Take brain breaks.** Your brain gets tired! Study for a little while, then take a short break to stretch, drink water, have a snack, or play for a few minutes. Then you can come back feeling fresh.

4.  **Sleep and be kind to yourself.** Getting a good night's sleep before the exam helps your brain remember everything you practiced. And if you get something wrong while practicing, that's okay! Mistakes just show you what to practice a little more.

Taking care of a pet is a big and important job, because a pet is a living friend who depends on you!

Think of it like taking care of a younger brother or sister. Here is what a pet needs every day:

**1. Food and Fresh Water**
Pets need healthy food every day, just like you need breakfast, lunch, and dinner. They also need clean, fresh water to drink all the time. Make sure to give them the right kind of food — dogs can't eat the same food as fish, and cats can't eat the same food as hamsters!

**2. A Clean and Safe Home**
Every pet needs a clean, cozy, and safe place to live. For a dog or cat, that means a warm bed and a clean house. For a fish, it means a clean fish tank. For a hamster or bird, it means a clean cage. You have to help clean up after them, too!

**3. Exercise and Playtime**
Pets get bored just like kids do! Dogs need walks and games of fetch, cats love to chase toys, and even hamsters need a wheel to run on. Playing with your pet keeps them happy, healthy, and makes them love you even more.

**4. Love and Attention**
Pets need lots of love! Talking to them kindly, petting them gently, and spending time with them makes them feel safe and happy. They will love you back a whole lot.

**5. Doctor Visits**
Just like you go to the doctor for check-ups, pets need to go to the animal doctor, called a vet. The vet makes sure they are healthy, gives them medicine to keep them from getting sick, and helps if they feel bad.

If you do all these things, you will be a great pet owner and your pet will be a happy, healthy best friend!

That is all for today

Sleep is like a superpower for your body and brain!

Think about your phone or tablet — when the battery gets low, you have to plug it in to charge overnight so it can work again the next day. Sleep is how YOU charge up.

Here is what happens while you sleep:

**1. Your brain gets smarter:** During the day you learn so many things at school and from playing. While you sleep, your brain sorts all that information and saves it, like filing papers into a folder. That helps you remember things better and solve problems easier.

**2. Your body grows and heals:** When you are asleep, your body makes special chemicals that help you grow taller and stronger. It also fixes any boo-boos and makes your muscles strong for running, jumping, and playing.

**3. It helps your mood:** Have you ever felt super grumpy and cranky when you didn't sleep enough? That's because your brain gets tired. A good night's sleep helps you feel happy, kind, and ready to have fun the next day.

**4. It keeps you from getting sick:** Sleep helps your body fight off germs, like little soldiers protecting you from colds.

Most kids your age need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep every night. That might sound like a lot, but that's what your amazing body needs to be ready for an awesome day of learning and adventure!

RIDING A BICYCLE IS LIKE LEARNING TO BALANCE AND HAVE FUN AT THE SAME TIME!

HERE IS HOW YOU DO IT:

1. GET YOUR HELMET ON! SAFETY FIRST. ALWAYS WEAR A HELMET TO PROTECT YOUR HEAD IF YOU FALL.

2. FIND A SAFE PLACE TO PRACTICE. A FLAT PARK OR AN EMPTY SIDEWALK WITH NO CARS IS PERFECT.

3. HOLD THE HANDLEBARS. THESE ARE WHAT YOU USE TO STEER LEFT AND RIGHT.

4. PUT ONE FOOT ON A PEDAL AND PUSH OFF WITH THE OTHER FOOT LIKE YOU ARE ON A SCOOTER. THIS GETS YOU MOVING!

5. ONCE YOU ARE MOVING A LITTLE BIT, PUT BOTH FEET ON THE PEDALS AND START PEDALING - THAT MEANS PUSHING THE PEDALS AROUND IN CIRCLES WITH YOUR FEET.

6. KEEP LOOKING FORWARD, NOT DOWN AT YOUR FEET. WHERE YOU LOOK IS WHERE YOU GO!

7. TO STAY UP, YOU NEED TO KEEP MOVING A LITTLE BIT. IT IS EASIER TO BALANCE WHEN THE WHEELS ARE SPINNING. IF YOU GO TOO SLOW, YOU WILL WOBBLE!

8. TO STOP, SQUEEZE THE BRAKES ON THE HANDLEBARS GENTLY. DO NOT SQUEEZE TOO HARD OR YOU WILL STOP SUPER FAST!

AT FIRST YOU MIGHT WOBBLE AND NEED SOMEONE TO HOLD THE BACK OF YOUR SEAT. THAT IS TOTALLY NORMAL! EVERYONE FALLS A LITTLE WHEN THEY LEARN. JUST KEEP TRYING AND SOON YOU WILL BE RIDING ALL BY YOURSELF AND IT WILL FEEL LIKE YOU ARE FLYING!

फ़ोन को आँखों से दूर रखो अंधेरे में फ़ोन मत देखो और एक जगह बैठे बैठे बहुत देर तक मत देखो बीच बीच में उठो टहलो और आँखों को आराम दो

३ अच्छी चीज़ें देखो
ऐसे खेल और वीडियो देखो जिनसे कुछ नया सीखने को मिले डरावनी या गंदी चीज़ें कभी मत देखो अगर कुछ अजीब लगे तो तुरंत माता पिता को बताओ

४ पढ़ाई और खेल को पहले रखो
पहले गृहकार्य खेलना और किताबें पढ़ना करो फिर फ़ोन चलाओ फ़ोन इनाम है काम नहीं

५ अनजान लोगों से बात मत करो
फ़ोन पर किसी अनजान व्यक्ति का संदेश आए या कोई नाम पूछे तो जवाब मत दो अपने माता पिता को दिखाओ

६ फ़ोन को सोते समय दूर रखो
रात को सोते समय फ़ोन को अपने पास रखकर मत सोओ इससे नींद खराब होती है

याद रखो स्मार्टफ़ोन तुम्हारा नौकर है मालिक नहीं जब तुम इसे समझदारी से चलाओगे तो यह तुम्हें बहुत कुछ सिखाएगा और मदद भी करेगा

पढ़ने के लिए धन्यवाद

- Replace incandescent bulbs with LED bulbs and turn off lights when leaving a room
- Unplug chargers, TVs, and small appliances when not in use to stop standby power
- Set your thermostat a few degrees lower in winter and higher in summer
- Wash clothes in cold water and run dishwasher and washer only with full loads
- Air-dry laundry and use natural daylight instead of electric lighting when possible
